# claude-supervisor

An MCP server + Claude Code plugin that lets one manager session spawn worker sessions and answer their permission prompts.

## What it provides

- MCP server `supervisor` with tools: spawn_agent, send_agent_message, list_agents, agent_status, pending_permissions, await_permission, answer_permission
- Slash commands: /supervisor:spawn, /supervisor:workers, /supervisor:answer, /supervisor:drain
- Session-finding commands: /supervisor:jump, /supervisor:who-needs-me (scripts/jump.py, scripts/who-needs-me.py; each resolves its location via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} with a ~/.claude fallback)
- Fleet commands: /supervisor:fleet-manager (stateful loop), /supervisor:fleet-status (read-only snapshot); helpers scripts/{fleet-sessions,box-table,fleet-snapshot,context-usage}.py
- Worker commands: /supervisor:worker-manager (stateful loop over ONE goal or topic), /supervisor:worker-status (read-only snapshot); helper scripts/open-items.py
- docs/fleet-surface.md is the canonical home for the spawn shape and the fleet table render spec
- Agent: supervisor:worker-wrangler (routine approval loop over headless workers, on a cheap model)
- Agent: supervisor:worker-sweep-reader (the worker sweep's read-only half — tracked-set read, bucket classification, id-set extraction, collision count, table render; called by both worker commands, never probes liveness and never acts)
- Skill: supervising-workers (when to delegate to a worker, which spawn mode to use, and how to run the loop)

## Two spawn modes

`spawn_agent` opens a worker either as a real `claude` session in a wezterm tab (`interactive: true`) or headless (`interactive: false`). Tooling is identical in both; the difference is who answers the worker's permission prompts and whether you can watch it.

The default is **fleet-wide and lives in a file**, not in the caller: omit the `interactive` argument and the server resolves `SUPERVISOR_SPAWN_MODE`, then `{"spawn":{"mode":…}}` in `~/.config/claude-supervisor/config.json` (`SUPERVISOR_CONFIG`), then its built-in `interactive`. Pass the argument only to force one worker against that default. An unknown mode value refuses the spawn; the file is read once at server start. `spawn_agent`, `agent_status`, `list_agents` and the ledger all report `mode_source` (`argument`/`env`/`config`/`default`).

## How a worker's permission prompt is answered

A **tab worker** answers its own prompts in its tab, so it never appears in `pending_permissions` — steer it with `send_agent_message` or drive its tab by hand.

⚠️ **`send_agent_message` is tab-only; ordinary cross-session `SendMessage` is not.** A headless worker has no pane for `send_agent_message` to type into, but it *is* reachable mid-task by plain `SendMessage`, in both directions (measured 2026-09-20). Read the limit as *"this tool cannot reach a headless worker"*, never as *"a headless worker cannot be reached"*.

A **headless worker** is a `query()` session from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk started with `permissionMode: 'default'`. Every approval-requiring tool lands in the server's `canUseTool` callback, which parks the request; the manager resolves it through `answer_permission`.

⚠️ **A headless worker DOES appear in `list_agents`** — this file claimed "it never appears in `list_agents`" until 2026-09-20, when a headless worker read its own roster row back (`personal-80 [fd6bbe] · interactive · busy`) and a manager session read the same row independently. It also holds a unix socket (`/tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock`). Two real limits replace the false one, and neither is invisibility: **the roster's mode column reports `interactive` for headless workers too**, so it cannot be used to tell the two apart; and **the roster is volatile** — 12 rows shrank to 8 within 17 minutes as workers exited at turn end — so any roster-derived conclusion needs a timestamp. To decide liveness, read the session registry (`~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`), which deletes an entry when its session exits.

**`agent_status` and `list_agents` also carry `current_tool_call`** — `{name, input_summary, started_at, held_seconds}`, the call the worker is inside right now and how long it has been held, or `null`. It is read from the worker's transcript, and it is the field that tells a long tool call apart from a worker parked on a gate: `session_status` says both are not-idle, this says *which* call and *for how long*. In flight means the **LAST** `tool_use` with no matching `tool_result` — an interrupted call leaves an unmatched `tool_use` behind, so "any unmatched `tool_use`" keeps naming calls the worker abandoned.

⚠️ **For an `AskUserQuestion`, answer with `deny` + a `message` — never `allow`.** An `allow` lets the tool run in a tty-less session, where it waits ~11 minutes and the worker exits with the question **unanswered**. The `message` carries the operator's answer in the form the question expects, prefixed `Operator answer, via supervisor:`. An `allow` is correct only for an ordinary tool-approval request, where the tool can actually run. Full spec, including the `spawn_agent(resume=…)` continuation that replaces this call once a worker has exited: `docs/fleet-surface.md` § A headless worker exits at turn end.

⚠️ The manager's outgoing `answer_permission` call is gated by the **manager session's own** permission mode, not the worker's. Under `auto` the classifier can refuse it (measured 2026-09-19) — the fix is Shift+Tab → `accept edits` in the manager session, then retry, never a change to the worker's mode or `defaultMode`.

## Install

/plugin marketplace add <owner>/claude-supervisor
/plugin install supervisor@claude-supervisor
